# Feasible endpoint enlargement with an exact cap signature

This is an actual finite-menu deformation in arbitrary continuous
dimension. Its availability condition is explicit: the added volume
must lie in one fixed strict cap-sign region, and the enlargement must
preserve midpoint compatibility. The theorem does not infer that such
a convex enlargement exists near every boundary point of a fiber.

## 1. Setting and actual enlargements

Let d>=1. Let A,K,B be d-dimensional convex bodies at integer bases
-1,0,1, with (A+B)/2 contained in K; these are the only integer fibers.
Every compatible enlargement below is realized by the convex hull of
the three labeled fibers: its fiber at 0 is exactly K by midpoint
compatibility, its endpoint fibers are the specified A_epsilon and B,
and its integer projection contains only -1,0,1.
Let y_0 belong to int K. Let v_0,...,v_d be nonzero spanning normals
with their sole dependence sum_i v_i=0. Put h_i=h_B(v_i),
b_i=2v_i.y_0-h_i. Suppose the caps

    v_i.(x-y_0)+(v_i.y_0-h_i)z>=0

all have the same raw mass Q, their A and K traces are proper, and
their B traces are supporting faces, hence have zero d-volume.
Define normalized section measures

    sigma_Ai=H_(d-1)(A intersect {v_i.x=b_i})/||v_i||,
    sigma_Ki=H_(d-1)(K intersect {v_i.x=v_i.y_0})/||v_i||,
    s_i=2sigma_Ai+sigma_Ki,
    lambda_i=1/s_i, Lambda=sum_i lambda_i.

All s_i are positive. The ordinary d=1 section convention is H_0=1
at a proper interior point.

Assume there is a sequence of convex bodies A_epsilon containing A,
with

    (A_epsilon+B)/2 subset K,
    delta_epsilon=|A_epsilon|-|A|>0, delta_epsilon ->0.

Let I be a nonempty index set. Require a fixed kappa>0 such that,
up to null sets, every point of A_epsilon minus A satisfies

    v_i.x>=b_i+kappa for i in I,
    v_i.x<=b_i-kappa for i notin I.                  (1)

Thus its ENTIRE added mass has one actual strict signature. For
nearby meeting points y, all these signs persist because the A cut
thresholds move to 2v_i.y-h_i. Write

    F_i(y)=|K intersect {v_i.x>=v_i.y}|
       +|A intersect {v_i.x>=2v_i.y-h_i}|.

The exact new budget is consequently

    F_i(y)+delta_epsilon 1_(i in I).                 (2)

This identity is why no differentiability of the body family itself
is required.

## 2. A common moving cap budget parameterized by added volume

The functions F_i are C^1 near y_0. At a proper cut, convex section
volumes are continuous in the threshold, and differentiation of the
cap integral gives

    grad F_i(y_0)=-s_i v_i.

In dimensions d>=2 the section continuity also follows from
Brunn--Minkowski concavity of their (d-1)-volume roots on the interior
projection interval. The d=1 case is elementary interval length.

Solve the d+1 equations

    F_i(y(delta))+delta 1_(i in I)=q(delta).

Their derivative in (y,q) is nonsingular. A kernel vector obeys
-s_i v_i.delta_y-delta_q=0; multiplying by lambda_i and summing gives
delta_q=0, and spanning then gives delta_y=0. The C^1 implicit-function
theorem therefore supplies actual y(delta) in int K and a common
budget q(delta), for all sufficiently small real delta, with

    y(0)=y_0, q(0)=Q,
    q'(0)=p_I:=sum_(i in I)lambda_i/Lambda>0.         (3)

To check the derivative, differentiate the budget equations and sum
with weights lambda_i; their y derivatives cancel by sum v_i=0.
For each available body A_epsilon, evaluate this same C^1 curve at
delta=delta_epsilon. Equation (2) shows that its actual displayed caps
all have budget q(delta_epsilon).

These caps cover the whole middle fiber: their middle inequalities
are v_i.(x-y(delta))>=0, and their sum cannot be strictly negative.
Thus every actual point of the middle fiber has true halfspace depth
at most q(delta_epsilon). The displayed caps need not remain critical.

## 3. Global-depth control, including a tied unchanged endpoint

Assume now that Q is the original globally maximal raw mixed depth.
Let m_A,m_B be the ordinary maximum raw halfspace depths of A and B,
and assume only

    m_A<Q.                                          (4)

The endpoint maxima in the exact three-fiber mixed set equal the
ordinary maxima, by finite integer-tilt isolation. Adding total mass
delta to A increases its ordinary maximal raw depth by at most delta:
for each fixed point of the original A this follows directly from
the cap inequality, but new possible points also require justification.

For that justification use ordinary depth regions. For every point
x of the ambient continuous space, not only x in A, its depth with
respect to the new A_epsilon measure is at most its depth with respect
to A plus delta. Outside A, separation gives old depth zero (a
supporting plane gives zero d-volume on the boundary). Inside A its
old depth is at most m_A. Therefore the new ordinary maximum is at
most m_A+delta. This handles newly available endpoint centers.

The unchanged endpoint has m_B<=Q, with equality permitted. Since
q'(0)=p_I>0, for sufficiently small positive delta,

    m_A+delta<q(delta),   m_B<=Q<q(delta).

The actual new globally maximal raw mixed depth is consequently at
most q(delta). With M=|A|+|K|+|B|, its normalized upper certificate has
derivative

    [q(delta)/(M+delta)]'_(delta=0)
       =(M p_I-Q)/M^2.                              (5)

Hence any available sequence of such enlargements yields strict
normalized descent whenever

    p_I<Q/M.                                        (6)

The endpoint B may be tied at the original global maximum; enlargement
raises the common menu budget to first order and increases the
denominator, so that fixed endpoint causes no source-switch problem.
For the planar bad-source branch in the small-endpoint note, the
separately proved a<b/6 and global comparison Q>=Gamma_2 b imply
m_A<=a<Q, so (4) is automatic there.

## 4. A concrete sufficient geometric availability condition

For a polytope A, the condition can be realized at an entire strict-
signature facet. Define the compact convex feasible enlargement body

    E={x:x+B subset 2K}=intersection_(b in B)(2K-b).

It contains A. Let F be a facet of A, and suppose all points of F
have the strict signature I with a uniform margin. Suppose there is
a point p in relint F that belongs to int E. Let n be the outward
unit normal to F. For sufficiently small epsilon>0, p+epsilon n
belongs to E and strictly satisfies every facet inequality of A
except the inequality defining F. Therefore

    A_epsilon=conv(A union {p+epsilon n}) subset E,

and its added part is exactly the pyramid over F with apex
p+epsilon n, apart from the base. Its volume is

    delta_epsilon=epsilon H_(d-1)(F)/d>0.

To see the pyramid assertion, any segment from the new point into A
first enters through F: the new point satisfies every other facet
inequality, and the segment keeps satisfying those inequalities.
Thus its portion outside A lies between the new point and F.
Conversely this entire pyramid lies in the hull. Since F is compact
and has a strict signature, the pyramid keeps a fixed positive
signature margin for all sufficiently small epsilon. All hypotheses
of Sections 1--3 follow.

Accordingly, at an attained below-target local minimum for which (4)
holds, a strict-signature facet with weight p_I<Q/M cannot have a
relative-interior point in int E. This is a scoped compatibility
contact conclusion about ACTUAL movable facets. It does not assert
the same conclusion for an arbitrary exposed vertex: a point bulge
at a vertex can expose distant adjacent faces with different
signatures. No unsupported localization of a convex enlargement is
used.
